text:
Happy Sunday! We're starting right around freezing, so expect some frost on the windshield, but plenty of sunshine takes over and the afternoon is a beauty, with a high near 61. A few high clouds slide in later ahead of a cold front, and a light south breeze picks up. It's a great day for a walk to catch the last of the fall color. Tonight won't be nearly as cold, with a low around 40.

Monday stays mild, near 60 in the NWS forecast, though some of the models run a few degrees cooler, with more clouds around. A shower or sprinkle is possible between 3 and 4 in the afternoon, but the air ahead of the front is so dry that I wouldn't bother with an umbrella. Then the switch flips. Tuesday only climbs into the 40s, with lows in the 20s, and Wednesday morning could be the coldest we've seen yet, in the lower teens to lower 20s, maybe flirting with a record. Enjoy a light jacket today, and dig out the heavy coat before Tuesday.

week.blurb: Sunny and mild after a chilly start, with a high near 61 and a dry evening, so enjoy the afternoon.

Sunny and noticeably colder, a high around 47, maybe a few degrees cooler, then a frosty night near 25.
Sunny and a little milder, with a high near 53 after a frosty morning, then clouds building overnight.
Mostly sunny and the warmest day of the week at 62, with a stray shower possible after 2 and into tonight.
Partly sunny with a high near 60, and a leftover shower is possible early in the morning, then dry.
Halloween looks partly sunny and mild, with a high near 61, so trick-or-treaters should be fine without heavy coats.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-25T06:12:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Mild temperatures expected today and Monday ahead of an approaching cold front.
  2. Cooler temperatures expected Sunday with warming temperatures through the remainder of the week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 212 AM EDT Sunday... No significant changes have been made with this forecast package.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Today will be a chamber of commerce type of day with high temperatures warming into the lower to mid 60s after a cool start to the morning. Light winds will switch to the south at 5-12 mph this afternoon. Plentiful sunshine will be seen through much of the day with high clouds filtering in ahead of the approaching cold front this afternoon. A cold front will move across the region Monday afternoon with the potential for isolated to scattered rain showers ahead of the boundary. Models continue to show a plethora of dry air in the low levels and the general idea is that the best chances for rain will be across the high terrain as it's unlikely we see the deeper valleys have time to saturate before dry air advects into the region in the wake of the cold front. Some of the high-res guidance is showing up to 0.05" of rain across the summits but even that seems a bit generous given the antecedent dry air mass. KEY MESSAGE 2: Noticeably colder temperatures will be observed on Tuesday and Wednesday as high pressure and clear skies will coincide with decent low level cold advection. Tuesday morning will see lows in the 20s while Wednesday morning will see lows in the lower teens to lower 20s. Highs on Tuesday will only climb into the 40s. It'll be our first real taste of arctic air this fall as the transition to winter isn't too far away. As a matter of fact, we may be looking at some record low temperatures Wednesday morning. The good news is that high pressure overhead will allow the air mass to slowly moderate Wednesday into next weekend with highs climbing back into the 60s for Thursday and Friday. There is a slight chance for a few showers on Friday with another weak cold front but again it looks like dry conditions will likely persist. For those with little ones who plan to go trick-or-treating, the forecast for Halloween looks dry and seasonably mild.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Sunday will continue the dry and sunny weather, except it will be pleasantly warmer with highs in the upper 50s to mid-60s. It will be excellent for checking out the remaining fall foliage. Though we’re past peak at this point, there are still some trees that have nice color. Sunday night won’t be as cold due to a gentle southwest breeze ahead of a cold front. That front will pass through mainly dry on Monday, but a few sprinkles are possible in northern parts of the region. Highs will be in the 50s. Much cooler air will move in behind this front. Tuesday will be a nice-looking day, but it will be quite chilly with highs only in the 40s. You’ll certainly want a jacket. Lows will be in the 20s, though some teens are likely. Wednesday will be a bit warmer with sunny skies and highs in the upper 40s to low 50s. Thursday will be pleasant with some low 60s expected. Another front will move through Thursday night. Some showers are possible along that, but no significant rain is expected. Any showers will end Friday morning, with the rest of the day being partly sunny and fair. Halloween looks good for trick-or-treaters with mostly sunny skies and highs mainly in the mid-50s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-24T22:27:00Z — same caveat): Warmer Sunday, continued wall-to-wall sun — Tonight will again be quite cold, due to clear skies and light wind. Temperatures fall back to the 20s and low 30s. Expect another round of frost and freeze conditions. High pressure stays nearby Sunday, bringing full sunshine! It turns warmer, thanks to a light south breeze that develops. Highs reach the mid-60s. An approaching cold front brings more clouds and a few spot showers for northern areas on Monday. Southern Vermont looks brighter overall. Highs will be near 60. Behind that front, a shot of unseasonable cold arrives Tuesday, as highs fall back to the mid-40s. Expect a mix of sun and clouds. Wednesday stays cool, with highs near 50 and a partly sunny sky. Another warmup arrives late week with highs near 60, thanks to a gusty south breeze. A few showers are likely later Thursday into Friday, with another cold front on approach, though not anticipating any significant rain. Halloween weekend looks dry and seasonable, with partly sunny skies and highs back near 60.
